Boruch Hashem
Blessed is He

# Production Live Evidence

The Awtsmoos opens not an imagined map but a public road of light;
Awtsmoos.com now answers crawler, reader, and Torah path in the same visible sight.

## Public crawler doors

Fresh direct HTTPS requests to the canonical origin proved:

- `https://awtsmoos.com/robots.txt` — HTTP 200, `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, advertising both sitemap URLs.
- `https://awtsmoos.com/sitemap.xml` — HTTP 200, `application/xml; charset=utf-8`, valid XML containing `/` and `/heichelos`.
- `https://awtsmoos.com/heichelos/sitemap.xml` — HTTP 200, `application/xml; charset=utf-8`, valid URL-set XML containing the public Ikar Heichel.

The root sitemap is intentionally a seed map. Deep discovery proceeds through ordinary server-rendered HTML links rather than an expensive recursive sitemap request.

## Public crawl graph

Fresh raw HTML proved:

- `/heichelos/ikar` has H1 `Ikar`, the semantic fallback marker, and two ordinary series links.
- the Likkutei Torah `שלח` series has H1 `שלח`, eighteen ordinary named-post links, and the target post link.
- no JavaScript execution is required for those discovery links to exist in source HTML.

## Public Road SSR

Fresh public raw HTML for numeric Road position 4 proved:

- HTTP 200;
- title `בפ' נסכים | Ikar | Awtsmoos`;
- H1 `בפ' נסכים`;
- canonical named-post URL ending in `BH_POST_1749784377821_theAlterRebbe_94`;
- robots `index,follow,max-image-preview:large,max-snippet:-1,max-video-preview:-1`;
- 16,527 characters of server-rendered Torah article text;
- normalized article SHA-256 `1f08e9709245f17eacb30baeb8732b7dde1505d8d7c4765e9825232bd0211f10`;
- no template, ReferenceError, or SyntaxError marker.

The stable named-post URL produced the same 16,527-character body and the exact same normalized SHA-256 hash.

A nonexistent named post produced `noindex,follow`, H1 `Torah teaching unavailable`, the missing-article marker, and no template error.

The final public assertion emitted `PUBLIC_REAL_DOOR_ACCEPTANCE_PASS`; both sitemap documents also parsed successfully as XML.

## Release infrastructure

Production activation initially exposed a stale tunnel-agent release manifest. The authoritative runtime collector expected 2,442 files while the checked-in witness omitted twenty-one runtime files.

The repository-native manifest builder regenerated version `1.0.575` from the authoritative catalog. Evidence before publication:

- 2,442 runtime files covered;
- ZIP/runtime probe passed;
- dedicated `test:tunnel-release` suite passed 23/23;
- the byte-identical regenerated manifest reached `main` and removed the production verifier blockage.

## Main branch reconciliation

At the final bounded synchronization check:

- local `/Users/Awtsmoos/Work/Awtsmoos.com` main SHA: `8c9dfc9ba4a4942c3042c6141fba20fa7d833b8e`;
- `origin/main` SHA: `8c9dfc9ba4a4942c3042c6141fba20fa7d833b8e`;
- targeted SEO/release paths were clean.

Earlier divergent local history was proven patch-equivalent upstream with `git cherry`; every unrelated dirty file was fingerprinted before reconciliation, and all 180 fingerprints remained unchanged after the safe `reset --keep` reconciliation.

## External cache note

An independent web/search fetch briefly continued showing the pre-deployment snapshot immediately after production flipped. Fresh direct HTTPS requests to the canonical origin already returned the new documents. Search-engine recrawl and cache refresh are external asynchronous processes and are not evidence that the origin remains stale.
